evidence.quoted_text:
drop: ${{ steps.monotonic.outcome == 'failure' }}
    steps:
      - name: Check out the repo (full history — the guard needs the base diff)
        uses: actions/checkout@fbc6f3992d24b796d5a048ff273f7fcc4a7b6c09 # v5.1.0 (immutable commit pin; repo policy)
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          # pnpm runs repo code below, so the checkout token must not
          # survive checkout (persist-credentials: false).
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Set up pnpm (version from package.json packageManager)
        # v6.1.0, immutable commit pin (repo policy)
        uses: pnpm/action-setup@ea17c68df8912ef543352723c149a84f56e3d413
      - name: Set up Node 24
        uses: actions/setup-node@a0853c24544627f65ddf259abe73b1d18a591444 # v5.0.0 (immutable commit pin; repo policy)
        with:
          node-version: 24
          cache: pnpm
      - name: Install dependencies
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
      - name: Build the CLI from source
        run: pnpm run build
      - name: 'Baseline monotonicity guard (CLI: ratchet.monotonicGuard)'
        id: monotonic
        continue-on-error: ${{ github.base_ref == 'main' }}
evidence.reason: The job output `drop` is computed solely from `steps.monotonic.outcome == 'failure'` (line 31), while line 54 sets `continue-on-error` for PRs to main, so a tolerated step failure is exactly what `drop` reports. The step can fail for reasons other than a real baseline loosening, such as a CLI crash, a missing tool, or the op returning `status: error`; the downstream issue can therefore claim a baseline was loosened when the guard merely failed. That contradicts the workflow's stated purpose of opening one issue when a main PR actually loosens a baseline.
